ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is an axisymmetric figure with line $AC$ as its axis of symmetry. If $\angle BAC = 65^\circ$ and $\angle B = 50^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle BAC=65^\circ$ and $\angle B=50^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BCA=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle BAC=180^\circ-50^\circ-65^\circ=65^\circ$,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is an axisymmetric figure,\\
therefore $\angle BCA=\angle DCA=65^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BCD=\angle BCA+\angle DCA=\boxed{130^\circ}$.
